entities.summary: Bérard de Got was a French bishop and Roman Catholic Cardinal, born into the noble family of Villandraut, and served as a key advisor to Pope Clement IV. He played a crucial role in the election of his brother, Bertrand de Got, as Pope Clement V, and was instrumental in shaping the Catholic Church's response to the Black Death. As a prominent figure in Western Europe during the 14th century, Bérard de Got's legacy extended beyond his own lifetime, influencing the development of the Church and shaping the course of European history. He was canonized as a saint by the Catholic Church in the 16th century, and his feast day is still celebrated by some Catholic orders today. His remarkable life serves as a testament to the enduring power of faith and family in shaping the course of human history.

entities.summary:
Bérard de Got, a French bishop and Roman Catholic Cardinal, played a pivotal role in shaping the medieval Catholic Church. Born in 1250 in Villandraut, France, de Got rose through the ecclesiastical ranks to become a cardinal, contributing to the Church's governance and liturgy.

As a key figure in the papal conclave of 1305, de Got participated in the election of Pope Clement V, a brother of his. His involvement in this event, however, was overshadowed by the tumultuous politics of the Papal States.

De Got's legacy extends to the impact of the papacy on Western Europe during the 14th century, a period marked by the Black Death and the rise of city-states.

The tumultuous politics of the Papal States and the power struggles within the Catholic Church left an indelible mark on the course of medieval history.

This Cardinal's involvement in the papal conclave of 1305 and his subsequent contributions to the governance of the Catholic Church demonstrate the intricate web of power and influence that defined the medieval era.
